principles: Nickel superalloys retain useful strength at temperatures where many structural alloys lose substantial strength.
Thermal conductivity is generally relatively low compared with aluminium and copper, so thermal gradients and machining heat must be considered.
CTE remains material- and temperature-dependent and must be combined with adjacent-material CTE in precision assemblies.
Oxidation and microstructural stability become coupled with thermal exposure.
rule: Do not extrapolate room-temperature datasheet values into hot-section analysis.
